newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia protests over Turkish buffer zone in Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Russia protests over Turkish buffer zone in Iraq.

text.p: Russia's Foreign Ministry said on Saturday that it was deeply concerned by Turkey's plans to set up a buffer zone in Kurdish areas of northern Iraq, Interfax news agency reported.
"Whatever the motivation is for this step, it is a serious violation of the territorial integrity of a sovereign state," the agency quoted a senior Foreign Ministry official as saying.
"In the present extremely tense situation in the region, such an action by Ankara can only destabilise the situation even further," he said.

Turkey has started a military build-up along its border with Kurdish-held northern Iraq ahead of creating a security zone up to 10 km (six miles) deep inside Iraq to check attacks by its own rebel Kurds.
The United States said on Thursday it did not object to the Turkish plan after Ankara said it would be temporary and not involve the stationing of Turkish troops.

Turkey says Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) rebels have increased activity in the volatile border region since Baghdad intervened in fighting between Iraqi Kurd rebels in northern Iraq and Washington fired cruise missiles at southern Iraq in retaliation.
Russia, which has generally taken a softer stance than the West on Iraq since the end of the 1991 Gulf War, denounced the U.S. missile attacks.
